title: CS 209: Java Basics
description: How Java runs, printing and concatenation, escape characters, variables and data types, division, IPO. Lectures 9-24, 9-29 and 10-1.

cards.definition: Java Virtual Machine: runs bytecode and produces the output.
Java Runtime Environment: the JVM plus Java's built-in libraries. Everything needed to RUN Java.
Java Development Kit: the JRE plus the compiler (javac) and dev tools. Needed to WRITE and compile Java.
What javac turns your .java source into (.class files). Platform-independent; the JVM runs it.
Runs in 2 stages: source → bytecode (compile time), then bytecode → JVM (runtime). Java is one.
Runs in 1 stage, line by line. Python is one.
Caught going from source to bytecode: syntax errors (missing ;), type mismatch, undeclared variable. The program never runs.
Happens while the bytecode runs on the JVM: file does not exist, no permission, divide by zero.
Everything between a pair of curly braces. Every { needs a matching }.
The program's entry point. public = visible anywhere, static = no object needed, void = returns nothing, args = command-line arguments.
Return type meaning the method returns nothing; it only executes.
println prints then moves to a new line (ln = line). print stays on the same line.
If either side of + is a String, + joins text instead of adding. Evaluated left to right.
A backslash makes the next character mean something special (or normal): \" quote, \\ backslash, \n new line, \t tab.
A note in the code that Java ignores, like # in Python.
A named memory location that stores a value of a specific data type.
Declare: int price;  Initialize: price = 2;  Both at once: int price = 2;
Primitive whole number, 4 bytes. e.g. 1, 2, 3, 5
Primitive number with a fraction, 8 bytes. e.g. 2.3. Storing 2 gives 2.0
Primitive true/false. Default false for fields (local variables have no default).
Primitive single character in single quotes, 2 bytes. e.g. 'a'. Each char has a number code ('A' = 65).
An object type (not primitive): a sequence of characters in double quotes.
Returns the remainder of a division. 15 % 2 is 1.
int / int gives an int: the fraction is dropped. 5 / 2 is 2.
If either side is a double, the result is a double (Java picks the bigger type). 5.0 / 2 is 2.5
Input → Process → Output. The way to plan a program before writing it.
Can contain digits but cannot START with one. Convention: start lowercase (camelCase).

questions.prompt: Which one do you need to WRITE and compile Java (not just run it)?
questions.explanation: The JDK = JRE + the javac compiler and dev tools. The JRE only runs Java.
The Java Virtual Machine runs bytecode, which is why the same .class file runs on any OS with a JVM.

questions.prompt: How many stages does a compiled language like Java run in?
questions.explanation: Stage 1: source → bytecode (compile). Stage 2: bytecode → JVM (run). Interpreted languages like Python use 1.

questions.prompt: Forgetting a ; at the end of a line is what kind of error?
questions.explanation: Syntax errors are caught by the compiler while turning source into bytecode, so the program never runs.

questions.prompt: Your program tries to open a file that does not exist. What kind of error?
questions.explanation: The code compiles fine; it only fails while running on the JVM.

questions.prompt: In public static void main, what does void mean?
questions.explanation: void is the return type: nothing comes back, the method only executes.

questions.prompt: Your class is public class Welcome. What must the file be named?
questions.explanation: A public class must match its file name exactly, and Java is case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Which line is a compile error?
questions.explanation: Single quotes are for ONE char only. 'hello' is not a valid char literal; Strings need double quotes.
No String is involved, so + adds the numbers.
The String comes first, so 1 and 2 are each appended as text, left to right.
Once a String is involved, everything after it is concatenated as text.
Left to right: 1 + 2 is added first (3), THEN joined to the String.
1+2 adds to 3, then everything is concatenated. A char joined to a String prints as the character.
print does not end the line, so the second print continues on the same line.
println ends the line after printing, so hi starts on a new line.
Each \" is an escaped quote, so the quotes print as normal characters.
Escape sequences are read in pairs: \\\\\\ is three \\ pairs = three backslashes. Then \"CS209\" prints the quotes.
\\ = one backslash, \n = new line, \t = tab, \" = quote. The last \\\\ is two backslashes.
// works like # in Python: the rest of the line is a note for humans.
Both are Strings, so + concatenates. Pure concatenation.
10 + 20 is pure addition (30) before the String shows up.
The String is first, so 10 and 20 are concatenated as text.
Parentheses are evaluated first, so 10 + 20 adds to 30 before joining the String.
* has higher precedence than +, so 5 * 2 = 10 happens first.
+ is evaluated left to right: "Cost: $" + 5 is a String, then + 2 appends text.
Parentheses force the addition first.

questions.prompt: Given int count = 4; what does this print?
questions.explanation: count is 4. String first, so 4 then 1 are appended as text.

questions.prompt: Given int count = 4; what does this print?
questions.explanation: The parentheses add count + 1 = 5 first.

questions.prompt: Given int count = 4; double price = 2.5; what does this print?
questions.explanation: Numbers come first, so 4 + 2.5 adds to 6.5 (a double, since one side is a double) before the String.
+ and - have equal precedence, left to right. "Result: " + 10 is a String, and you cannot subtract 5 from a String, so it does not compile.
% (modulus) gives the remainder: 15 / 2 is 7 remainder 1.
Integer division: int / int gives an int, and the .5 is dropped (not rounded).
double / double gives a double.
double / int gives a double: Java uses the bigger type (8 bytes over 4).
5 / 2 is integer division (2) BEFORE it is stored. Storing 2 in a double makes it 2.0.
x is 2.0, and 2.0 / 2 is 1.0 (double / int gives a double).

questions.prompt: Which line is a compile-time error?
questions.explanation: You cannot put a fraction into an int (it would lose data). Putting 2 in a double is fine: it becomes 2.0.
A local variable must be given a value before it is used, or the compiler refuses.

questions.prompt: price = 2; (with no int price anywhere) — what happens?
questions.explanation: Every variable must be declared with a type first.

questions.prompt: How many bytes is an int?
questions.explanation: int = 4 bytes, double = 8, char = 2.

questions.prompt: How many bytes is a double?
questions.explanation: double = 8 bytes, which is why it wins when mixed with an int.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a primitive type?
questions.explanation: String is an object type. The primitives here are int, double, boolean and char.

questions.prompt: What values can a boolean hold?
questions.explanation: boolean is true/false only. Its default (for fields) is false.
A char prints as the character itself, exactly as stored (lowercase stays lowercase).
Storing a char in an int keeps its number code. 'A' is 65.
It is stored as an int, so it prints the number 75. You only get K if it is a char: char c = (char) ('A' + 10);
75 is the code for K, and casting to char prints the letter.

questions.prompt: Which variable name is NOT allowed?
questions.explanation: A name can contain digits but cannot start with one.

questions.prompt: For an average calculator, which step is 'calculate and store the average'?
questions.explanation: IPO: Input (3 numbers) → Process (compute the average) → Output (print it).
125 / 60 = 2 (integer division) and 125 % 60 = 5 (the remainder). This is the seconds-converter IPO from class.
